description:
Found while trying to byte-fingerprint products for fz-go4.18.28.1 (base 0cb890e95, release fz2 interp --dump). (1) backend dump: 4 base runs of map_enumerable produce 4 DIFFERENT dump hashes -- backend program content (lane/shape id numbering, entry lists) varies per run, making byte-level product fingerprinting impossible. (2) activations dump: Kernel.dbg/1([int]|[]) return type flips between '[int] | []' and 'int | float | binary | atom | opaque | brand | var | any | ... ' across runs of fz_f98_range_map_converges AT BASE (hashes c43e0bd4/0eafbf4e both observed from the base binary and from the fz-go4.18.28.1 binary) -- the ReturnType fixpoint end-state is schedule-dependent, and one of the two states is a WIDENED (any-carrying) return. Interp outputs are stable; the wobble is in the settled fact/product content. Related: the 'backend callable N ambiguous across callable entries [..]' failure ids on the take-family fixtures (00419/00420) also vary run to run. Diagnose with the minimal-job-trace gate; the widened-dbg state may also be a correctness/perf signal (any-lane boxing).

NEW OBSERVATION (fz-go4.18.28.8, 2026-07-02, at 8cdbf0439): 00277_enum_tier0_fixture is now ALSO run-to-run nondeterministic in final output/exit status -- intermittent 'backend executable N failed to decode input... backend expected runtime lane 2', reproduced at similar rates on both the pre-fix and post-fix binaries (not caused by .28.8's change). Previously only 00420/behavior-take-drop-split were confirmed flaky; this widens the affected set to at least 3 fixtures. Production TIMING itself (gap-sums) was stable and unaffected across .28.8's before/after measurements -- only the final decoded-output/exit-status layer is schedule-dependent, consistent with the ReturnType-fixpoint-widening theory above (a lane/shape numbering wobble surfacing as a runtime decode mismatch downstream). This strengthens the case that this ticket's root cause is upstream of backend production (in the settle/fixpoint layer, not the artifact/backend job code .28.7/.28.8 touched).

NEW EVIDENCE (fz-go4.24, 2026-07-03): 00277's base-binary nondeterminism includes an ANSWER CONFLATION, not just decode aborts -- three consecutive base runs gave three different outputs, including a run where the Enum.reduce(xs,0,+) sum and the Enum.count(xs,pred) count printed each other's answers (one of the pair prints the other's result), alongside the known intermittent 'backend expected runtime lane 2' decode abort. A schedule-dependent WRONG-ANSWER (not just a crash) strengthens the case that the ReturnType/lane-numbering wobble reaches semantic routing, consistent with this ticket's widened-return theory and .28.5's wait-order dependence. After fz-go4.24's clause hygiene, 00277 completes more often but the conflation remains -- it is upstream of the types-persistence layer.
